answer.rationale: One decision this cycle. Finance mandates 18% spend cut and contract expires in 14 days. I cannot both switch vendors (onboarding risk at 94% line utilization, no buffer) and add a second source. Deferring is not viable—the contract does not auto-renew, so inaction means supply stops. Memory c4 shows renegotiation at renewal recovered real margin via benchmarking; memory c6 shows multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing without narrowing service scope. Selecting memory_c6 for verification because it is the one record that directly tests whether locking a multi-year deal with the incumbent can deliver the 18% unit-cost reduction finance requires while keeping delivery continuity intact (no migration, no interruption). If verified, I will open a renewal negotiation with the incumbent offering a multi-year term in exchange for volume pricing and improved payment terms, targeting the 18% cut without introducing any new-supplier onboarding risk on a line already at 94% with no buffer.
